notes.title: “Born of water and the Spirit”
notes.intro: Jesus tells Nicodemus that no one can enter the kingdom of God unless born of water and the Spirit.

views.label: Water refers to baptism, which gives new birth
views.summary: Catholic, Orthodox and Lutheran Christians, with many early church writers, read “water” as baptism, through which the Spirit gives new birth.
views.source: Catechism of the Catholic Church 1215, 1257; Luther’s Small Catechism on Baptism

views.label: Water refers to baptism as the response of faith
views.summary: Churches of Christ also see baptism here, as part of the believer’s response that God uses for new birth.
views.source: Everett Ferguson, The Church of Christ (1996)

views.label: Water refers to physical birth or to cleansing by the Spirit
views.summary: Many evangelicals read “water” as natural birth or as a picture of the Spirit’s cleansing (Ezekiel 36:25–27), so new birth is the Spirit’s work received by faith.

notes.common: All agree that new birth is God’s work by the Holy Spirit.
